questions.question_text: Why can a medicine lose potency when stored in a hot, humid place contrary to its label?
questions.option_a: Heat and moisture can accelerate its degradation
questions.option_b: The label's ink reacts with the active ingredient
questions.option_c: Humidity changes every medicine into a gas
questions.option_d: Warmth permanently increases all drug activity
questions.explanation: Storage conditions affect chemical stability and shelf life.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which measure most directly prevents cross-contamination between raw poultry and cooked food?
questions.option_a: Use the poultry board for cooked food without washing
questions.option_b: Use separate clean utensils and preparation surfaces
questions.option_c: Rinse both foods in the same bowl
questions.explanation: Separate equipment and cleaning reduce pathogen transfer.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A bulging sealed food can should be treated as unsafe because it may indicate
questions.explanation: Gas formation and package swelling can signal microbial spoilage; do not taste suspect food.

questions.question_text: A broad-spectrum antibiotic should not be self-prescribed for every sore throat because
questions.option_a: antibiotics work only by lowering temperature
questions.option_c: broad-spectrum drugs have no side effects
questions.option_d: many sore throats are viral and antibiotics can cause harm and resistance
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses; inappropriate use contributes to resistance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a drug's generic name from a brand name?
questions.option_a: Different brands can contain the same active ingredient
questions.option_b: A brand name guarantees a different molecule
questions.option_c: A generic medicine has no active ingredient
questions.option_d: Every brand name means the product is a vaccine
questions.explanation: The generic name identifies the active ingredient; brands are commercial names.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is a topical antiseptic not automatically suitable for disinfecting drinking water?
questions.option_b: It may not be approved or dosed for potable-water treatment
questions.explanation: Only products approved for drinking-water treatment should be used at specified doses.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.explanation: Drowsiness can impair reaction time and safe operation of vehicles.

questions.question_text: Why does a permitted preservative not guarantee that food can never spoil?
questions.option_a: Its effect is limited by formulation, dose, microbes and storage
questions.option_c: Food spoilage is unrelated to microbes
questions.option_d: A preservative turns food sterile at any concentration
questions.explanation: Preservation slows specified spoilage processes under intended conditions but has limits.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
